stories.headline: Anthropic says an unreleased Claude raised a Riemann zeta bound from 41.6% to 67.2%

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said on August 10 that an unreleased research version of Claude improved the longstanding unconditional lower bound for the fraction of Riemann zeta zeros on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%, while failing at the Riemann hypothesis itself
key_facts.excerpt: An unreleased research version of Claude has improved on a longstanding lower bound for the fraction of zeros of the Riemann zeta function that satisfy the Riemann hypothesis... increased this bound from 41.6% to 67.2%.

key_facts.fact: The result came out of two Claude Code sessions totaling 31 million output tokens after staff member Jarred Sumner, a non-mathematician, asked Claude to 'take a real stab' at the Riemann hypothesis
key_facts.excerpt: An unreleased research version of Claude found the new lower bound over two sessions in Claude Code, using a total of 31 million output tokens.

key_facts.fact: Claude first generated 650 ideas that failed, then spent about a day and a half coordinating roughly 60 subagents that ran about 2,400 shell commands, wrote hundreds of Python scripts and refereed each other's work
key_facts.excerpt: Initially, Claude generated and tried 650 ideas, none of which worked... it spent a day and a half coordinating about 60 Claude subagents... between them, they ran 2,400 shell commands and wrote hundreds of Python scripts.

key_facts.fact: Claude's subagents downloaded 54 arXiv papers to check the result was new, searched for counterexamples and re-proved the finding from scratch; Claude then recommended a human number theorist validate it
key_facts.excerpt: Claude tested its work by having various subagents review the proofs, search for counterexamples, download 54 papers from the arXiv to check that its finding hadn't already been made, and independently re-prove its finding from scratch.

key_facts.fact: The paper is authored by the model itself and states results of at least 67.250% of zeros being simple and on the critical line and at least 83.625% being distinct, accompanied by a Lean 4 formalisation
key_facts.excerpt: The author of this paper is a large language model developed by Anthropic... with an optimised test family the three constants become 0.6725, 0.6725, 0.83625... A Lean 4 formalisation of Theorems A–E accompanies the paper.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic mathematicians Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman reviewed the argument and outside number theorists Brian Conrey and Dan Goldston examined the paper on short notice; it has not been through conventional peer review
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic mathematicians Levent Alpöge and Ralph Furman subsequently analyzed the argument and its relationship to previous research. Conrey and Goldston, experts in the area, also examined the paper on short notice.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says it does not expect Claude's method to lead directly to a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and 67.2% does not mean the remaining zeros lie off the line
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic said it does not expect Claude's method to lead directly to a proof of the Riemann hypothesis... It improves a mathematical guarantee: at least 67.2% of the relevant zeros satisfy the condition required by the hypothesis.

stories.headline: OpenAI ships GPT-5.6-Cyber, a model trained to refuse fewer hacking requests, behind a vetted tier

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced on August 10 that it is splitting its Daybreak cybersecurity program into two access tiers: Daybreak Blue for frontier general-purpose models with defensive safeguards and Daybreak Red for purpose-trained cyber models
key_facts.excerpt: Daybreak Blue provides access to frontier general-purpose models, including GPT-5.6 Sol... Daybreak Red provides access to our purpose-trained cybersecurity models for authorized vulnerability research, exploit validation, and security testing.

key_facts.fact: GPT-5.6-Cyber, built on GPT-5.6 Sol and available through Daybreak Red, is trained to find zero-day vulnerabilities and develop exploit chains and to reduce refusals on higher-risk dual-use tasks
key_facts.excerpt: Built on GPT-5.6 Sol, it is trained to improve capabilities on several specialized cybersecurity tasks (e.g., finding zero-day vulnerabilities and developing exploit chains) and to reduce refusals for certain higher-risk, dual-use cyber tasks.

key_facts.fact: On OpenAI's internal Advanced Cybersecurity Completion Rate evaluation, GPT-5.6-Cyber answers 95.0% of exploit-chain, authentication-bypass and privilege-escalation requests, versus 57.3% for GPT-5.5-Cyber, 2.0% via Daybreak Blue and 1.5% for standard GPT-5.6 Sol
key_facts.excerpt: GPT‑5.6‑Cyber completes 95.0% of these requests, compared with just 1.5% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, and 2.0% when used with Daybreak Blue access... GPT‑5.5‑Cyber, which completes only 57.3% of requests.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says the model analyzed Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine and found two previously unknown vulnerabilities that can be chained to corrupt memory and bypass the V8 heap sandbox; Google patched them under CVE-2026-15903
key_facts.excerpt: the model analyzed V8, Chrome's JavaScript engine, and found two previously unknown vulnerabilities that can be chained together to corrupt memory and bypass the V8 heap sandbox. Google fixed the flaws after coordinated disclosure and assigned them the CVE-2026-15903 designation.

key_facts.fact: Access is gated by identity verification, monitoring, approved-use restrictions and legal attestations, and hardware security keys become mandatory for Daybreak accounts on September 1, 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Getting into either tier requires identity verification, account security measures, monitoring, and legal declarations. Hardware security keys become mandatory for all Daybreak accounts on September 1, 2026.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI rates both GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6-Cyber as High for cybersecurity capability under its Preparedness Framework but below the Critical threshold, and says GPT-5.6-Cyber was not involved in the Hugging Face exploitation incident
key_facts.excerpt: we also evaluated its frontier cyber capabilities and determined that it similarly reaches the High threshold but not the Critical threshold... GPT‑5.6‑Cyber was not involved in exploiting Hugging Face, nor are any other models planned for an upcoming release.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI launched Daybreak in May, shortly after Anthropic launched its own cybersecurity coalition, Project Glasswing, and the expansion follows AI-model security incidents disclosed by OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta in recent weeks
key_facts.excerpt: Back in June, OpenAI first introduced Daybreak alongside GPT-5.5-Cyber, giving selected security researchers access to the stronger cyber capabilities of frontier models under additional safeguards.

stories.headline: Anthropic will watermark every Claude text output worldwide to comply with the EU AI Act

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said in a help document published Monday that generated text from new Claude models will carry embedded watermarks and generated files will include digitally signed provenance metadata, as part of complying with the EU AI Act's transparency rules
key_facts.excerpt: "Generated text will carry embedded watermarks, and generated files will include digitally signed provenance metadata where supported," the company said in a help document published on Monday.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic signed the EU AI Act's Article 50(2) Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content; Claude models launched on or after August 2, 2026 support machine-readable marking at launch, and earlier models are being retrofitted during the transition period
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has signed the EU AI Act Code of Practice on transparency for AI-generated content... Claude models that launch in the EU on or after August 2, 2026, will ship with this labeling baked in.

key_facts.fact: The marking applies globally rather than only in the EU, covering the Claude API, Claude, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and Claude Tag, plus Claude models served through AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Foundry
key_facts.excerpt: "Marking will apply to output from supported models wherever Claude is offered, worldwide."... This also includes third-party providers of Anthropic models like AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry.

key_facts.fact: Text carries an imperceptible watermark woven into the text itself that travels with copy-paste and 'may persist through some editing'; supported files (.svg, .png, .jpg) get signed metadata following the C2PA standard
key_facts.excerpt: The watermark will also move with text even if it is copied, pasted elsewhere, and lightly edited. Anthropic further noted that when Claude generates a supported file type (.svg, .png, or .jpg), signed provenance metadata will be attached.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic concedes a detected mark is not conclusive evidence Claude wrote the content, since users also have Claude proofread or translate their own text, and that absence of a mark does not prove human authorship
key_facts.excerpt: a watermark doesn't prove Claude wrote the content, since people often use the AI to edit or translate their own text. Heavy editing or format changes can also strip the markings entirely.

key_facts.fact: The detection tool that would let third parties check for the mark has not yet shipped, and Anthropic has not published the watermarking algorithm or a false-positive rate
key_facts.excerpt: The detection tool that would let anyone check for the mark has not yet shipped.

key_facts.fact: EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations became applicable on August 2, 2026, requiring providers to mark generative AI outputs including text in a machine-readable format
key_facts.excerpt: These transparency obligations, applicable from 2 August 2026... Outputs of AI systems (audio, image, video, text) are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated.

stories.headline: Anthropic signs a $9.1B, 20-year compute lease with bitcoin miner Riot Platforms

key_facts.fact: Riot Platforms disclosed on August 10 a 20-year lease for 191 MW of data center capacity at its Rockdale, Texas campus with an unnamed 'leading frontier AI lab'; Bloomberg identified the customer as Anthropic
key_facts.excerpt: Riot disclosed the deal on Monday, describing the counterparty only as a "leading frontier AI lab." Riot's Rockdale, Texas, campus will supply 191 megawatts of IT capacity under the terms of the 20-year lease, which extends through June 2048.

key_facts.fact: The contract runs through June 2048 and is expected to generate $9.1 billion in revenue for Riot; two five-year extension options could raise the total to $16.1 billion
key_facts.excerpt: Riot confirmed the agreement in an August 10 statement, noting that it is entering a 20-year contract with Anthropic that will run through June 2048. The deal is expected to generate $9.1 billion in revenue for Riot over the initial term.

key_facts.fact: Capacity comes online in stages: 96 MW by December 2027 and the full 191 MW by June 2028; the 191 MW is roughly the power draw of about 143,000 homes
key_facts.excerpt: Under the agreement, Riot will provide 191 megawatts (MW) of data center capacity from its Rockdale campus in Texas. The capacity is roughly equivalent to the electricity used by about 143,000 homes at any given time.

key_facts.fact: Riot stock jumped more than 25% after hours on Monday and was up around 21% in premarket trading on Tuesday
key_facts.excerpt: Following the news, Riot's stock rose over 25% in after-hours trading. As of press time, Riot was up 21.29% in overnight trading.

key_facts.fact: Riot, a bitcoin miner that mined 1,587 bitcoin in the second quarter of 2026, has now signed 241 MW of data center leases worth about $9.8 billion in six months, the other tenant being AMD
key_facts.excerpt: Riot Platforms is a bitcoin miner by heritage... having mined 1,587 bitcoin in the second quarter of 2026 alone... "executed leases totaling 241 megawatts of capacity, representing approximately $9.8 billion of long-term, contracted revenue".

key_facts.fact: Riot arranged a $573 million interim financing facility through Morgan Stanley to fund the project's early construction phase
key_facts.excerpt: To fund the project's early construction phase, Riot arranged a $573 million interim financing facility through Morgan Stanley as it works toward putting a permanent credit backstop in place.

key_facts.fact: The lease is Anthropic's third major compute procurement in three months, taking its commitments past $60 billion
key_facts.excerpt: For Anthropic, the deal represents its third major compute procurement in three months, totaling over $60 billion in commitments.

stories.headline: OpenAI buys back $7B in employee shares at a flat $852B valuation, using its own cash

key_facts.fact: OpenAI completed a secondary share sale of roughly $7 billion on Monday, letting current and former employees sell stock at the company's $852 billion valuation
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI completed a secondary share sale totaling roughly $7 billion, allowing current and former employees to sell stock at the company's $852 billion valuation, CNBC confirmed on Monday.

key_facts.fact: The $852 billion price is unchanged from OpenAI's record $122 billion funding round that closed in March 2026, the first flat print across its run of tenders
key_facts.excerpt: Each of those increased the number. This one didn't. $852 billion in, $852 billion out, the first flat print across OpenAI's run of tenders.

key_facts.fact: Unlike prior tenders that brought in outside buyers such as Thrive Capital and SoftBank, OpenAI funded this buyback with its own cash, according to two people familiar with the terms
key_facts.excerpt: In its last two employee tenders, OpenAI brought in outside buyers, Thrive Capital and SoftBank among them, to purchase the shares. This time, according to two people familiar with the matter, OpenAI used its own cash.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI filed its IPO prospectus confidentially with the SEC in June 2026 and has not disclosed a listing date; analysts read the tender and flat price as a sign an IPO is not imminent
key_facts.excerpt: The company also filed confidentially with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June to prepare for a potential IPO later this year. However, a tender offer suggests that an IPO may not be forthcoming soon.

key_facts.fact: Previous tenders were $6.6 billion at a $500 billion valuation in October 2025 and $1.5 billion in 2024, when OpenAI was worth $157 billion
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI ran a $6.6 billion employee sale in October 2025 at a $500 billion valuation... Before that, a smaller $1.5 billion tender to SoftBank in November 2024, when the company was worth $157 billion.

key_facts.fact: The tender was first reported by Bloomberg and confirmed by CNBC; OpenAI declined to comment
key_facts.excerpt: The $7 billion figure was first reported by Bloomberg... OpenAI submitted its IPO prospectus to the Securities and Exchange Commission under confidential cover in June without disclosing when it might actually list.

stories.headline: Anthropic cancels the September price increase and makes Claude Sonnet 5's $2/$10 pricing permanent

key_facts.fact: Anthropic said on August 10 it is making Claude Sonnet 5's introductory pricing permanent, keeping $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens
key_facts.excerpt: We're making Claude Sonnet 5's introductory pricing permanent.

key_facts.fact: The introductory price had been scheduled to run only through August 31, after which it was set to rise
key_facts.excerpt: We launched Sonnet 5 in June at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through August 31, and that price will remain unchanged.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic launched Sonnet 5 in June, pitching it as its most agentic Sonnet, able to make plans, use browsers and terminals and run autonomously at a level that until recently required larger, more expensive models
key_facts.excerpt: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5, our most agentic Sonnet yet. It makes plans, uses tools like browsers and terminals, and runs autonomously at a level that just a few months ago required larger and more expensive models.

stories.headline: Nvidia releases Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open 30B agent model, plus an open model router

key_facts.fact: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 3 billion active parameters, built for high-volume, low-latency execution in always-on AI agents
key_facts.excerpt: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is a 30B parameter, open Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 3B active parameters, specifically optimized for high-volume, low-latency execution in always-on AI agents and agentic workflows.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia says Lightning delivers up to 4x faster output than comparable models in its class and completes agentic tasks roughly 30% faster than Qwen3.6-35B at matching accuracy
key_facts.excerpt: According to Nvidia, Lightning delivers up to 4x faster output than comparable models in its class, completing agentic tasks roughly 30% faster than Qwen3.6-35B at matching accuracy.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the model Nvidia released NeMo Switchyard, an open-source routing library that sends each step of an agent workflow to the most suitable model; Nvidia says the pairing holds frontier-level task completion while cutting benchmark costs to roughly a third of running Opus 4.8 alone
key_facts.excerpt: Paired through Switchyard, Nvidia says the combination holds frontier-level task completion while cutting benchmark costs to roughly a third of running Opus 4.8 alone.

key_facts.fact: Weights, training data and recipes are released under the permissive OpenMDW-1.1 license, with the model on Hugging Face, ModelScope, OpenRouter and build.nvidia.com as an NIM microservice
key_facts.excerpt: the weights, training data, and recipes are released as permissively as possible under OpenMDW-1.1... try it on build.nvidia.com or through OpenRouter. Download the weights from Hugging Face, and ModelScope.

key_facts.fact: Switchyard partners include agent frameworks Cognition, LangChain and Nous Research, and LLM gateways Kong, LiteLLM and OpenRouter, which have built support into their products
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia split its partners into two groups: agent frameworks that call Switchyard directly, including Cognition, LangChain and Nous Research, and LLM gateways that have built Switchyard support into their own products, including Kong, LiteLLM and OpenRouter.

key_facts.fact: The model extends the hybrid Mamba-Transformer latent MoE architecture Nvidia introduced with the Nemotron 3 family, and is designed for agent harnesses like OpenClaw and Hermes Agent
key_facts.excerpt: It is designed for harnesses like OpenClaw and Hermes Agent—all supported by the NVIDIA NemoClaw open source security and management stack for running always-on AI agents.
